comparator.name: Human Movement Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page and the programme's version-1.0 2026-2027 curriculum poster jointly account for 180 EC. Year 1 comprises twelve 5-EC foundations. Year 2 comprises eleven 5-EC courses, a 3-EC orientation course and a 2-EC longitudinal Bachelor Monitor. Year 3 comprises 15 EC of genuine minor space, five named 5-EC courses and a 20-EC Bachelor Afstudeer Project. The programme has no named formal route requiring selection. The poster resolves two labelling problems in the public page's parsed table by identifying Neuroanatomie 2 and Statistiek 3 explicitly.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines functional anatomy and human physiology with neurobiology, perception and action, movement-related health, mathematical signal methods, programming, imaging and data analysis. It offers a coherent route into human-movement questions while retaining the absence of Groningen's dedicated biomechanics, exercise-physiology laboratories, movement-analysis practica and 20-EC movement-science research project.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed courses span bodily function, brain and action, health, quantitative models and research methods; the title does not imply Groningen's specialist biomechanics or sport-performance sequence.

alternatives.concept: A distinct route generated by the programme's exercise-and-health and sport-psychology interests. It explores movement and recovery through brain and behaviour, anatomy, physiology, medical and clinical psychology, development and philosophy of mind and emotion. It retains data and experimental research but gives more space to behavioural health and rehabilitation than to mechanical and signal modelling.

alternatives.labelRationale: The title reflects the route's actual combination of movement-relevant body and brain study with health, behaviour and psychology; it does not claim clinical or sport-psychology qualification.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Four courses in the measurement-focused route (linear algebra, numerical methods, signal systems and probability theory) give way to abnormal psychology, psychodiagnostics, philosophy of mind and philosophy of emotion. This is a substantive 30-EC shift from physical quantification toward behavioural health and recovery, while shared anatomy, brain and research foundations remain visible.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The integrated anatomy, brain, measurement and health curriculum is the closest feasible response, although Groningen's biomechanical and exercise-specific laboratory progression remains unmatched. A second evidence-backed route shifts exactly 30 EC from physical quantification to behavioural health and recovery; it is substantively distinct and feasible. A proposed sports-performance and talent-development route would require a coherent set of specialised exercise physiology, training-load, sport-performance and biomechanics courses that the UCR workbook does not provide, so no third 24-course alternative is claimed.

notes.text: Groningen requires specialist biomechanics, exercise physiology, movement analysis and measurement practicals, plus a 20-EC empirical movement-science project. UCR offers functional anatomy, general physiology, neuroscience, psychology and quantitative/data methods without reproducing that specialist laboratory progression. Groningen's 15-EC minor remains open in the comparator.
